chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man insulted the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) during the time of Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). He was brought to the governor of Medina, who gathered the people. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered upon him, and he was near the time of his illness, wearing a red-bordered robe. They seated him in the front of the gathering and asked his permission to recline. He said to them, "What do you think?" Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and al-Hasan ibn Zayd and others said to him, "We think his tongue should be cut." The governor turned to Rabi'ah al-Ra'i and his companions and said, "What do you think?" He said, "He should be disciplined." Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, "Glory be to Allah! Is there no difference between the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his companions?'"

key_terms.رَبِيعَةَ الرَّأْيِ: Rabi'ah of opinion (a title for a jurist/official)

ai.seo_question: What was the punishment for insulting the Prophet Muhammad according to the governor's officials in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s critical engagement with the Umayyad judicial system, where he challenges the inconsistency between the severe punishment for insulting the Prophet and the lenient treatment of insults against his companions. By asking 'What do you see?' and noting the lack of distinction, Imam al-Sadiq highlights the theological principle that the Prophet’s honor is intrinsic and distinct, thereby critiquing the arbitrary application of *ta'zir* (disciplinary punishment) by the state. This incident underscores the Imam’s role not just as a spiritual guide but as a juristic authority correcting legal precedents based on prophetic precedent.
